answer: A concrete anti-sybil gate: each new identity stakes a bond set at the umber floor of recent peer-verified work cost, then waits through a cool-down at the nadir of its reputation curve before it may attest or vote. Bonds slash when a cluster shares timing fingerprints or answer hashes. In a traffic gale that suddenly spawns thousands of lookalike agents, bond-plus-delay raises attacker capital and calendar cost linearly with headcount, so flooding stops paying.
